It's time to get rid of it, and 1-800-GOT-JUNK? is here to help. Disposing of an old bicycle can be a bit tricky, but with the right information and assistance, you can ensure it's recycled responsibly. ### Understanding the Challenges of Bike Disposal - Bicycles are made up of various materials, including metal, plastic, rubber, and other components. - Some parts, like tires and chains, may be recyclable, while others, like the frame, may not be. - Bike donations may not always be accepted by local charities, and improper disposal can lead to waste in landfills. ### Donation Options for Old Bicycles Donating your old bicycle to a local charity or non-profit organization is a great way to give back to the community while keeping your bike out of a landfill. Some popular options include: - The Salvation Army - Goodwill - Local cycling clubs Before donating, make sure the organization you choose accepts bicycles and that they'll be properly recycled or sold to fund their programs. ### Recycle Your Bike: Metal and Component Recycling Some parts of your old bicycle, such as the frame, wheels, and gears, can be recycled. You can: - Check with local recycling centers to see if they accept bike parts - Contact local bike shops or manufacturers to see if they have a bike recycling program - Consider partnering with a bike recycling organization to collect and process bike donations ### Proper Disposal for Unacceptable Bike Components If certain parts of your bike can't be recycled, it's essential to dispose of them properly to prevent environmental harm.
